explain.say: Picture stone walls taller than a three-storey house, made of granite blocks fitted so well that no cement holds them together. That is Great Zimbabwe, in southern Africa. Its story runs along this timeline. Let's walk it.

explain.say: See the castle? In the 1300s builders made the Great Enclosure, with walls up to 11 metres tall, using no mortar, which is the sticky paste that holds bricks. They just stacked granite very carefully. Could you build a wall with nothing gluing it?

faq.a: Ancestors of the Shona people, a Bantu-speaking people of southern Africa, built it from about 1100 to 1450 CE. Archaeology firmly shows it was African-built.

faq.q: How were the walls built without mortar?
faq.a: Builders split granite into neat blocks and stacked them carefully, tilting the walls slightly inwards for balance. This dry-stone method needs no cement.
asks: What holds Great Zimbabwe's walls up?

faq.q: Who did Great Zimbabwe trade with?
faq.a: Its gold and ivory went to Swahili coast ports like Kilwa. In return came cloth, glass beads from Persia and India, and porcelain from China.
Nobody is fully sure. Likely reasons include too many people for the land and water, and trade moving to other centres. By about 1450 most people had left.
asks: Why did people leave Great Zimbabwe?

faq.q: Why did people deny Africans built it?
faq.a: In colonial times some Europeans, and later the white Rhodesian government, wrongly claimed outsiders built it, to justify their rule. In 1929 the archaeologist Gertrude Caton-Thompson showed it was African.
asks: Why was Great Zimbabwe's history hidden?

facts: The Great Enclosure's walls reach about 11 metres high and use no mortar.
Great Zimbabwe became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
The soapstone Zimbabwe Bird found at the site appears on Zimbabwe's flag.

quiz.say: What holds Great Zimbabwe's walls together?
quiz.show: The walls stay up because of…
quiz.why: Granite blocks were stacked so well that they balance without mortar.

wrong.1: No cement or mortar was used at all.
wrong.2: No metal bolts hold the stones.

quiz.say: What does the name Zimbabwe mean?
quiz.why: The name comes from Shona words meaning houses of stone.

wrong.1: The city traded gold, but the name means houses of stone.
wrong.2: The name refers to stone buildings, not a river.
